description: Free public phone numbers from many countries, with every incoming text shown live on the page.

name: Recommend Me a Book
description: Read the opening page of a random novel with title and author hidden, and only reveal them if it hooks you.

name: Sketchfab
description: Spin and inspect millions of 3D models in the browser, from museum scans and fossils to game art. Many are free to download.

name: SoundboardGuys
description: Thousands of meme, prank and celebrity sound buttons to click through or download.

name: Sprite Fusion Destroy
description: Type in any web address and the page turns into a pixel-art level you can smash apart, alone or with friends.

name: Staggering Beauty
description: Wiggle your mouse at a black worm and keep shaking it. Best avoided if flashing lights bother you. A useless-web classic.

name: SwissTransfer
description: Send files up to 50 GB without an account, kept for thirty days, run by a Swiss cloud company.

name: TasteDive
description: Name a band, film, book or game you love and get a list of similar things across all of them.

name: Temp Number
description: Public temporary phone numbers whose incoming SMS show up on the page, for sign-ups you don't want your real number on.

name: Terraink
description: Make minimalist map posters of any city, styled to taste and exported print-ready as PNG, PDF or SVG.

name: Thiings
description: Over ten thousand 3D object icons in one cheerful style, free to search and download.

name: TinyWow
description: Hundreds of single-purpose PDF, image and video tools behind one search box, free and without an account.

name: Toy Theater
description: Simple maths, reading and art games for young children, with virtual manipulatives that teachers actually use in class.

name: TypingBird
description: Typing lessons and arcade-style games that build speed and accuracy, gentle enough for kids.

name: UI Colors
description: Type in one brand colour and get a full Tailwind-style shade scale from 50 to 950, ready to copy.

name: VibeSail
description: A 3D sailing simulator where trimming the sails actually matters. Daily races, real coastlines and short tutorials on how wind works.

name: WiFi Map
description: Over a hundred million crowd-sourced Wi-Fi hotspots and passwords on a map, handy when abroad.

name: WiFi Space
description: A world map of Wi-Fi hotspots with their passwords, shared by travellers.

name: Workout Cool
description: Build workout routines from a large exercise library and track your progress. Free, ad-free and open source.

name: Yarn
description: Search a quote and get the exact clip from films, shows and music videos, ready to share as a link or GIF.

name: YOUDJ
description: A two-deck DJ mixer in the browser that plays tracks straight from YouTube and SoundCloud, with crossfader, loops and effects.

name: Your AI Slop Bores Me
description: Type a prompt and a human, not a model, answers it. A funny and rather sweet protest against generated everything.

name: Murdoku
description: Place the suspects on the crime scene and reveal the killer. Play free online, print puzzles, or get the best-selling Murdoku books.

name: MTV REWIND
description: The classic MTV experience, back and streaming 24/7. No reality shows, no ads, just music.

name: Agar.io
description: Be a cell, eat smaller cells, avoid bigger ones. The game that started the whole .io genre is still running.

name: AirConsole
description: Open it on a laptop or TV and everyone's phone becomes a controller. Instant local multiplayer for a room full of people, nothing to install.

name: Animagraffs
description: Long animated infographics that take apart a car engine, a fire truck or a city's water system and show every moving piece working.

name: Animated Drawings
description: Upload a child's drawing of a person or creature and it gets a skeleton, then walks, jumps and dances. A research demo from Meta.

name: Anime.js
description: A small JavaScript animation library with a homepage that shows off what it can do. Timelines, staggering and SVG morphing with a pleasant API.

name: AutoDraw
description: Scribble a lopsided bicycle and a neural net offers clean drawings of bicycles by real illustrators to swap in. A Google experiment.

name: Bomomo
description: A row of strange brushes that swarm, orbit and bounce after your cursor, leaving patterns you could never draw yourself.

name: Bundlephobia
description: Type an npm package and see what it costs your users: minified and gzipped size, download time, and lighter alternatives, before you install it.

name: Can I email
description: Like Can I use, but for email clients. Look up any HTML or CSS feature and see whether Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail will actually render it.

name: cobalt
description: Paste a link from YouTube, TikTok, SoundCloud and many others and save the video or audio. No ads, no tracking, nothing else on the page.

name: Color Hunt
description: A hand-picked feed of four-colour palettes, voted on by designers. Scroll, click a swatch to copy its hex code, move on.

name: dbdiagram.io
description: Type tables and relations in a tiny markup language and watch the entity-relationship diagram draw itself next to your code.

name: Decker
description: A HyperCard-style multimedia sketchbook with 1-bit graphics. Draw cards, add buttons and a little scripting, and you have a zine, a game or a tool.

name: DeepL Translator
description: Translations that read as if a person wrote them, with alternative phrasings one click away. The one to use when tone matters.

name: Devhints
description: Hundreds of one-page cheatsheets for languages, frameworks and CLI tools, written to answer the question you have right now and nothing more.

name: DiceBear
description: Turn any username into the same friendly avatar every time, in dozens of styles from pixel art to hand-drawn faces. Free API, libraries and a playground.

name: Draw a Stickman
description: Draw your own stick figure hero, then draw keys, fire and boats to get them through the adventure.

name: Drive From Home
description: Pick a city and ride along on a real drive through its streets while local FM radio plays. Armchair travel through a thousand cities.

name: Dungeon Scrawl
description: Draw dungeon and battle maps for tabletop games in a hand-inked old-school style. Rooms, corridors and hatching snap into place, no sign-up.

name: FakeUpdate
description: Full-screen fake update screens for every version of Windows, macOS and more, complete with a progress bar that never finishes.

name: Azgaar's Fantasy Map Generator
description: Generate a whole fantasy world with continents, rivers, nations, cultures and trade routes, then edit every detail. Worldbuilders' favourite.

name: fffuel
description: Dozens of small SVG generators for gradients, noise, squiggles, blobs and textures, each one playful enough to lose half an hour in.

name: Fontjoy
description: Press generate and get a heading, subheading and body font that work together. Lock the one you love and let it find partners for it.

name: Fontshare
description: Distinctive typefaces from the Indian Type Foundry, free for personal and commercial use, with a type tester and web embed for each one.

name: Fragrantica
description: An encyclopedia of perfume, with notes, accords and longevity for tens of thousands of fragrances, voted on by people who wear them.

name: FreeSewing
description: Enter your measurements and get made-to-measure sewing patterns for shirts, trousers, coats and more. Volunteer-run and free.

name: generals.io
description: Fast real-time strategy on a grid hidden in fog. Grow your army, take cities, and find the enemy general before they find yours.

name: Goblin Tools
description: Small helpers built for neurodivergent brains. Magic ToDo breaks a scary task into tiny steps, and others judge the tone of a message or estimate time.

name: grep.app
description: Search a million public GitHub repositories at once, with regex, in milliseconds. The quickest way to see how real code uses a function or config option.

name: Haikei
description: Generate layered waves, blobs, blurred gradients and low-poly backgrounds as SVG. Every shape has sliders and a randomise button.

name: Hero Patterns
description: A collection of subtle repeating SVG background patterns. Choose colours and opacity, then copy a single line of CSS.

name: Hoppscotch
description: Send REST, GraphQL and WebSocket requests straight from a browser tab. A fast, self-hostable alternative to Postman that opens instantly.

name: HTTP Cats
description: A cat photo for every HTTP status code, served at http.cat/404 and friends. Half joke, half the reference you end up linking in API docs.

name: What Did Hubble See on Your Birthday?
description: Pick a day and month and NASA shows you the Hubble image taken on that date, with a short note on what you're looking at.

name: Huemint
description: Generates palettes previewed on a website, a logo or a gradient, so you judge colours where they will be used. Lock the ones you like and reroll the rest.

name: Icônes
description: Search more than a hundred open-source icon sets at once and copy any icon as SVG or a framework component. Fast, keyboard-friendly, no install.

name: iFixit
description: Step-by-step photo guides for opening and repairing almost anything, from phones to washing machines, written by a community of fixers.

name: Jackson Pollock
description: Move your mouse and paint drips across the screen, faster for thinner lines. Click to change colour. An internet art piece from 2003 that still works.

name: JKLM.FUN
description: Fast party games for friends or strangers. In Bomb Party, type a word containing the given letters before the bomb goes off.

name: JustDeleteMe
description: Direct links to the account deletion page of hundreds of services, rated from easy to impossible, so you know what you're in for.

name: JWT.IO
description: Paste a JSON Web Token to decode its header and payload and check the signature. The first tab everyone opens when auth goes wrong.

name: Khroma
description: Pick fifty colours you like and a small neural net in your browser learns your taste, then generates endless palettes to match.

name: Kleki
description: A painting app in a browser tab with natural brushes, layers and filters, and an interface uncluttered enough to just start drawing.

name: Learning Synths
description: Ableton's playful course on synthesizers. Each lesson changes one knob on a synth in your browser, so you hear what oscillators, envelopes and filters do.

name: Little Alchemy 2
description: Start with air, earth, fire and water and combine them into hundreds of things, one discovery at a time. A calm puzzle you keep coming back to.

name: Logoipsum
description: Lorem ipsum for logos: a stack of believable fake brand marks to drop into mockups until the client finally sends theirs.

name: make 8-bit art!
description: A cheerful little pixel-art canvas by Jenn Schiffer. Pick a colour, pick a brush size, draw, save as PNG.

name: Math is Fun
description: Plain-language, illustrated explanations of maths from counting to calculus, with puzzles and little interactive tools. Still the clearest on the web.

name: Mathigon
description: An interactive maths textbook that talks back, plus Polypad, a virtual box of tiles, dice and number bars to explore ideas with your hands.

name: McBroken
description: A live map of which McDonald's ice cream machines are broken right now, found by a bot that keeps trying to order a McFlurry everywhere.

name: Method of Action
description: Tiny games that train a designer's eye: kern the letters, trace curves with the pen tool, match the colour. You get scored against a professional.

name: Mockaroo
description: Describe the fields you need and get a thousand rows of believable fake data as CSV, JSON or SQL, from names and addresses to IBANs and car models.

name: MuscleWiki
description: Click a muscle on the body map and get exercises for it, each with a looping video of how to do it properly.

name: Music-Map
description: Type a band and it floats in a cloud of similar artists, the closest ones nearest. A simple, surprisingly good way to find your next favourite.

name: musictheory.net
description: Short, clear lessons on notes, scales and chords, plus drills and ear trainers. The site music teachers have pointed students to for twenty years.

name: My90sTV
description: Flip through channels on a chunky old TV playing nineties shows, ads and music videos. Channel surfing without the cable bill.

name: Ninite
description: Tick the Windows apps you want and get one installer that sets them all up silently, declining every toolbar. The first thing to run on a new PC.

name: The Observatory of Economic Complexity
description: Treemaps of what every country makes and trades with everyone else. Click Chile and see copper. Click Japan and see cars.

name: OneLook
description: A reverse dictionary: describe a word you can't remember and it finds it. Also searches a thousand dictionaries at once and finds rhymes and related words.

name: Open Peeps
description: A hand-drawn library of people you assemble from heads, bodies, faces and poses. Released into the public domain, so use them anywhere.

name: OpenStax
description: Peer-reviewed college and high-school textbooks from Rice University, free to read online or download. Physics, biology, economics and more.

name: PairDrop
description: AirDrop for every device. Open the page on two phones or laptops on the same network and send files peer to peer, nothing stored on a server.

name: Papermau
description: A blog gathering thousands of free paper models from designers around the world: aircraft, buildings, robots, dioramas and odd little machines.

name: PaperMe
description: Make and print any kind of paper: lined, dotted, isometric, Cornell notes, guitar tabs or calligraphy grids, with every size and spacing adjustable.

name: Perchance
description: Thousands of community-made random generators for names, plots, monsters and prompts, plus a tiny language to build your own in minutes.
Slide numbered tiles and merge them until you reach 2048. The original, by the developer who made the game that ate 2014.

name: Pomofocus
description: A clean Pomodoro timer in a tab with a short task list. Start, work, take the break it gives you.

name: Project Euler
description: Hundreds of maths problems you can only solve with code, where the brute-force answer takes a week and the clever one takes a second.

name: Quick, Draw!
description: You have twenty seconds to draw a prompt while a neural network guesses out loud. Then see how millions of others drew the same thing.

name: React Bits
description: Over a hundred animated React components, from text effects to WebGL backgrounds, each with a live preview and props to play with before you copy it.

name: readme.so
description: Click together a README from ready-made sections like installation, usage and license, edit them side by side with a preview, and copy the Markdown.

name: Realtime Colors
description: Try a colour scheme and fonts on a full sample website instead of isolated swatches. Randomise, lock, check contrast and export when it looks right.

name: Sakugabooru
description: An archive of standout cuts of hand-drawn animation, tagged by animator, studio and show. Where animation fans go to study a single scene.

name: Servier Medical Art
description: Thousands of clean medical and biology illustrations, from cells to organs to lab gear, free to use in slides and papers under CC BY.

name: Settei Dreams
description: An archive of the model sheets animators work from, with character turnarounds, props and expression charts from decades of anime.

name: Shadertoy
description: Thousands of GPU shaders running live in the browser, from fractal landscapes to whole demoscene worlds in a few hundred lines. Fork any of them and tweak.

name: Sketch Toy
description: Draw something and share it as a replay, so the person you send it to watches every stroke appear in order.

name: Slow Roads
description: Drive an endless, procedurally generated road through forests, deserts and coastlines. No goal, no score, just the road and some music.

name: Space Type Generator
description: Type a word and bend it into spinning coils, ribbons and stacked loops of kinetic type. A playground for motion typography with endless sliders.

name: Sporcle
description: Timed quizzes on everything, from naming every country to every Best Picture winner, mostly made by players. One more quiz is always there.

name: Supercook
description: Tick off what is in your fridge and cupboard and it finds recipes you can make right now without going shopping.

name: TETR.IO
description: A slick, competitive block-stacking game with ranked matches, 40-line sprints and a calm zen mode. Plays like a native app in a tab.

name: The Colors of Motion
description: Every frame of a film averaged to one colour and laid out in a strip, so you can see the mood of a whole movie at a glance.

name: The Toymaker
description: A long-running collection of printable paper toys, boxes and cards to cut, fold and glue, all drawn by one illustrator with a lot of charm.

name: tixy.land
description: A 16 by 16 grid of dots driven by one line of JavaScript. Change the formula and the grid comes alive. Tiny, endlessly fiddly.

name: trace.moe
description: Drop in a screenshot from an anime and it tells you the show, the episode and the exact second it is from.

name: Transform
description: Paste JSON and get TypeScript types, a Go struct or a Zod schema back. Dozens of one-way converters between the formats you keep retyping by hand.

name: Typatone
description: Every letter you type plays a note, so writing a sentence turns into a small melody. From the makers of Patatap.

name: TypeLit.io
description: Practise typing by retyping classic novels chapter by chapter. Your speed improves and you finish Alice in Wonderland along the way.

name: Uiverse
description: A community gallery of buttons, loaders, toggles and cards made in plain CSS or Tailwind. Copy the code of any one you like, no attribution needed.

name: unDraw
description: A big library of flat illustrations for any idea. Set your brand colour before downloading and every one of them matches it. No attribution required.

name: Vocal Remover
description: Drop in a song and get the vocals and the instrumental as separate tracks. Also has pitch, tempo and key tools for karaoke and practice.

name: Watabou's Procgen Arcana
description: Procedural generators for medieval cities, villages, dungeons and neighbourhoods, each drawn in a lovely ink-on-parchment style.

name: Wheel of Names
description: Type some names, spin the wheel, get a winner. The classroom and giveaway favourite, with sounds, confetti and shareable wheels.

name: Wokwi
description: Wire an Arduino, ESP32 or Pico on a virtual breadboard, flash real firmware and watch LEDs blink and displays light up, with no hardware on your desk.

name: Wormhole
description: Share files up to 10 GB with end-to-end encryption and a link that expires on its own after a day. No account.

name: ZType
description: A space shooter where every enemy is a word and typing it is how you fire. Gets frantic fast, and it quietly makes you a better typist.

name: Bubble Cam
description: Watch the live BubbleCam and press the Bubbles button to send a real blast of bubbles into Andie and Mike’s South Florida backyard. Sending Bubbles Worldwide Since 2001

name: DH Tools
description: 46+ free online tools: PDF compressor, photo background remover, AI OCR table extractor, code formatter.

name: Jitter
description: Jitter is a collaborative motion design tool that lets you create professional animations in minutes, no matter your experience with motion.

name: Floor796
description: A huge animation scene with many references to memes, games, films, series, anime, music groups

name: play_music_theory
description: A visual instrument. Draw, and it plays.

name: Dither
description: Load an image or generate a gradient, then dither it with Bayer patterns, halftones or crosses in a GameBoy or CGA palette. Exports as SVG, so the dots stay crisp at any size.

name: Detexify
description: Draw the symbol you cannot name and it hands you the LaTeX command for it. Solves in five seconds a problem that otherwise eats twenty minutes of searching.

name: BetterExplained
description: Maths taught the way it should have been the first time: intuition and analogy first, formulas afterwards. The essays on e and the Fourier transform are the classics.

name: Web Design Museum
description: Thousands of screenshots of websites, apps and Flash games from 1991 onwards, so you can see exactly what Google, Netflix or Apple looked like the year you first used them.

name: Lospec
description: The reference library for pixel art: thousands of curated colour palettes, plus a browser pixel editor, dithering tools and tutorials for working under tight constraints.

name: Damn Interesting
description: Meticulously researched long-form stories about obscure corners of science and history, published slowly since 2005 and worth every month of the wait.

name: The Marginalian
description: Maria Popova's decades-long reading diary: long, careful essays threading poets, scientists and letter-writers together, with no ads and no sponsors of any kind.

name: Low-tech Magazine
description: A magazine about old and stubbornly durable technology, served from a solar-powered box in Barcelona. When the battery runs low the images dither and the site goes offline.

name: Ptable
description: The interactive periodic table everyone ends up linking to. Drag the temperature slider to watch the elements melt and boil, or switch to orbitals, isotopes and compounds.

name: xeno-canto
description: A community archive of wildlife sound: hundreds of thousands of bird, bat and insect recordings from around the world, searchable by species and shared under Creative Commons.

name: Heavens-Above
description: Give it your location and it gives back the exact time, direction and brightness of the next ISS pass, plus charts for satellites, comets and planets. Plain and trustworthy.

name: Reactor Atlas
description: Every nuclear reactor on earth on one map: what type it is, when it came online, how much power it makes, and which ones were shut down and why.

name: Chronotrains
description: Pick any European station and watch the map bloom outwards, shaded by how far you can get by train in one to five hours. Ruinous for an afternoon of work.

name: Freesound
description: A twenty-year community archive of field recordings, foley and loops, every one of them Creative Commons licensed and searchable by tag, length or sample rate.

name: NTS Radio
description: Two live channels out of London plus a decade of archived shows, hosted by people with unreasonably deep record collections and no algorithm anywhere near it.

name: myNoise
description: Background noise generators with a slider per frequency band, so you can tune rain or a distant train to mask exactly the sound your room has too much of.

name: Cookie Clicker
description: The idle game that started the whole genre. Click a cookie, buy a grandma, and discover several hours later that the grandmas have gone somewhere very dark.

name: skribbl.io
description: Free multiplayer Pictionary with no account and no install. Make a private room, send the link, and everyone is drawing badly within about fifteen seconds.

name: Gartic Phone
description: Telephone played with drawings: you write a sentence, someone draws it, someone else describes the drawing. The album it plays back at the end is the whole point.

name: Newton's Orchard
description: A gravity sandbox in the browser. Fling planets at each other, watch orbits settle or collapse, and get an intuition for the n-body problem by wrecking it.

name: WindowSwap
description: Ten minutes out of a stranger's window, somewhere in the world. Uploaded by whoever lives there, with the birds and the traffic left in.

name: DOS Zone
description: Ultimate collection of free dos games to play online in browser. No registration needed, no advertisment, just play!

name: A Dark Room
description: A text game that opens with a single button — stoke the fire — and slowly becomes something much larger and stranger. Play it before reading anything about it.

name: archive.today
description: Paste a URL and it freezes the page as both a screenshot and a text copy that stays up after the original goes down. Catches plenty the Wayback Machine misses.

name: Atlas Obscura
description: A gazetteer of the world’s overlooked places — a stairwell to nowhere, a museum of soil, a town built inside a rock. Browsable as a map or as very good writing.

name: Bruno Simon
description: A developer portfolio you drive around in a toy truck, knocking over the CV as you go. The most quoted argument that WebGL was worth learning.

name: Cameron's World
description: One endlessly scrolling collage built entirely from images and text salvaged from GeoCities before it was deleted. Under construction, forever.

name: Compiler Explorer
description: Type code on the left, watch the assembly appear on the right, colour-matched line by line, across dozens of compilers. The fastest way to see what yours actually does.

name: Nullschool Earth
description: A live globe of wind, ocean currents, waves and particulates, animated straight from forecast data. Spin it, switch the layer, and watch the weather move.

name: iNaturalist
description: Photograph anything alive and a mix of naturalists and machine vision will tell you what it is. Verified sightings become open biodiversity records scientists actually use.

name: IT Tools
description: A drawer of small developer utilities — hashes, JWT decoding, cron parsing, colour conversion, QR codes — in one tidy interface you can also self-host.

name: Our World in Data
description: Long-run data on health, energy, food and poverty, charted and sourced, with the underlying numbers downloadable. The place to check a claim about how the world is going.

name: PhET Interactive Simulations
description: Hundreds of physics, chemistry and biology simulations you can poke at — drag a mass onto a spring, mix a solution, build a circuit and watch it burn out.

name: Piskel
description: A pixel-art and sprite-animation editor that runs in the tab, with onion skinning and GIF export. Everything you need to make a walk cycle and nothing you do not.

name: Poolsuite FM
description: An endless summer radio station wrapped in a System 7 interface, with VHS holiday footage playing in a little window. Formerly Poolside FM, still ridiculously good fun.

name: Red Blob Games
description: Amit Patel’s interactive explainers on pathfinding, hex grids, noise and map generation. The A* article alone has taught a generation of game programmers.

name: Regex Crossword
description: Crossword puzzles whose clues are regular expressions, starting gentle and ending somewhere near cruel. The most painless way to actually learn the syntax.

name: Seeing Theory
description: Probability and statistics taught as things you drag: sample from a distribution, watch a regression line settle, see the central limit theorem happen in front of you.

name: SomaFM
description: Listener-supported internet radio out of San Francisco: forty-odd hand-curated channels, no adverts, running since 2000. Groove Salad has outlasted most streaming services.

name: Standard Ebooks
description: Public domain books rebuilt properly: proofread text, modern typography, real covers, no scan artefacts. What Project Gutenberg files look like after a copy editor.

name: Submarine Cable Map
description: Every fibre-optic cable on the ocean floor, drawn on one map with its landing points, owners and dates. The physical internet, suddenly legible.

name: The Pudding
description: Visual essays answering questions nobody thought to ask — how pockets differ by gender, what makes a rap lyric rhyme. Journalism you scroll through rather than read.

name: Zooniverse
description: Real research projects that need human eyes: classify galaxies, transcribe ship logs, count penguins. Ten minutes of your attention becomes a line in someone’s paper.

name: Yan
description: Yan is a glitch art photo editor with 36+ algorithms: pixel sort, CRT scanlines, RGB shift, ASCII, Risograph and 1-bit dither. Free on iOS and Android, plus 25 texture filters that run entirely in your browser with zero

name: playgrnd
description: 32 free, single-purpose generative design tools. No accounts, no uploads, everything runs in your browser.

name: Airport Simulator
description: A browser-based air-traffic game inspired by Flight Control: drag planes to runways and keep the airport moving without collisions.

name: TimeGuessr
description: Read a historical image for its time and place, then pin your best guess on the map in a daily geography challenge.

name: Ambiphone
description: Ambient music + sounds for work, study and relaxation

name: Fonts In Use
description: An indexed archive of typography in the wild, searchable by typeface, format and industry.

name: NASA Eyes
description: Fly through a real-time 3D model of the solar system, tracking actual spacecraft on actual trajectories.

name: Flightradar24
description: Every aircraft in the sky right now, clickable, with routes, aircraft type and altitude.

name: Windows 93
description: A fake, hostile, hilarious operating system running in your browser with real working nonsense apps.

name: Ableton Learning Music
description: Make a track in your browser while learning what beats, chords and basslines actually do.

name: Cryptopals
description: Crypto challenges that teach you how ciphers break by making you break them yourself.

name: Coolors
description: Generate colour palettes by hitting spacebar until something clicks, then lock, tweak and export.

name: remove.bg
description: Cuts the background out of an image in about three seconds, usually better than you would by hand.

name: Public APIs
description: A gigantic curated list of free APIs, sorted by category, with auth and CORS support noted for each one.

name: Google Arts & Culture
description: Gigapixel scans from the world museums, plus tours, stories and some genuinely fun experiments.

name: Every Noise at Once
description: An algorithmically generated scatter plot of every musical genre Spotify knows, each one playable.

name: freeCodeCamp
description: Thousands of hours of coding curriculum, entirely free, with certifications and real projects.

name: GeoGuessr
description: Dropped somewhere in Street View, guess where on earth you are. Bollards become important.

name: Setosa — Explained Visually
description: Hard statistics concepts turned into things you can drag: eigenvectors, conditional probability, PCA.

name: DevDocs
description: Documentation for hundreds of APIs in one fast, searchable, offline-capable interface. Entirely keyboard driven.

name: Marginalia Search
description: A search engine that deliberately favours small, non-commercial, text-heavy sites. Finds the old web.

name: Wikipedia
description: The improbable success story of the internet. Start anywhere; you will be somewhere else in an hour.

name: Stellarium Web
description: A planetarium in your browser showing the sky above your exact location, right now.

name: Silk
description: Draw symmetrical, glowing, silk-like patterns that look far better than your actual drawing skill.

name: Who Can Use
description: Shows how a colour pair looks to people with different vision types, not just a single ratio number.

name: Zoomquilt
description: An infinitely zooming painting, hand-assembled from panels that loop seamlessly forever.

name: Type Scale
description: Pick a ratio and preview a whole typographic scale in your own font, then copy the CSS straight out.

name: Down for Everyone or Just Me
description: Settles the argument about whether the site is down or your wifi is broken.

name: Windy
description: Animated wind, rain and temperature layers over the whole planet, with genuinely useful forecasts.

name: AlternativeTo
description: Crowdsourced alternatives to any piece of software, filterable by licence and platform.

name: Chrome Music Lab
description: Thirteen tiny experiments that teach rhythm, harmony and spectrograms by letting you poke at them.

name: Advent of Code
description: A December calendar of programming puzzles with a story, a leaderboard and a devoted community.

name: web.dev
description: Guidance on performance, accessibility and modern browser capabilities, straight from the Chrome team.

name: Khan Academy
description: Free, structured courses from arithmetic to art history, with practice that adapts to you.

name: Shields.io
description: Concise, consistent and legible badges for your README, generated from live data about your project.

name: Are.na
description: Collect and connect images, links and text into channels. A calm, ad-free alternative to moodboards.

name: Radio Garden
description: Spin a globe and listen to live local radio from anywhere on earth. The best map on the internet.

name: The Public Domain Review
description: Essays curating the strangest and loveliest things that have fallen out of copyright.

name: Monkeytype
description: A minimal, deeply customisable typing test with beautiful themes and obsessive statistics.

name: The Evolution of Trust
description: A playable introduction to game theory that explains why cooperation appears, and why it collapses.

name: crontab.guru
description: A cron schedule expression editor that translates five cryptic fields into a plain English sentence.

name: WebAIM Contrast Checker
description: Paste two colours, get the WCAG contrast ratio and a pass or fail. The definitive quick answer.

name: Observable
description: Reactive notebooks for data analysis and visualisation, with a huge public gallery to learn from.

name: Old Maps Online
description: Search historical maps by place and date across hundreds of library collections at once.

name: This Is Sand
description: Pour coloured sand into dunes with your cursor. Meditative in a way no productivity app manages.

name: Zoom Earth
description: Live satellite imagery, storm tracks and wildfire data on a smooth, fast globe.

name: Pointer Pointer
description: Move your mouse anywhere and a photo of a person pointing at exactly that spot appears.

name: Squoosh
description: Compress images with a side-by-side slider so you can see exactly what quality you are trading away.

name: Placehold.co
description: Placeholder images straight from a URL, with size, colours, format and text all set as parameters.

name: patterns.dev
description: A free book on design patterns and component patterns for modern web apps, with runnable examples.

name: Privacy Guides
description: Non-hysterical, well-researched recommendations for private tools and sensible threat models.

name: Rainy Mood
description: Rain and thunder, looping forever. The original ambient noise site, and it is still running.

name: Grid Garden
description: The same trick as Froggy, but for CSS grid. Water your carrots with grid-column-start.

name: Internet Arcade
description: Thousands of real arcade cabinets emulated in the browser, preserved by the Internet Archive.

name: Wolfram Alpha
description: A computational knowledge engine that answers questions with worked steps rather than links.

name: Carbon
description: Turn source code into a beautiful image for slides and posts, with real syntax themes and window chrome.

name: MetaFilter
description: A community weblog running since 1999 where the best of the web gets posted and discussed.

name: explainshell
description: Paste a shell command and get every flag and argument annotated with the matching line from the man page.

name: Open Library
description: One web page for every book ever published, with borrowing built on the Internet Archive.

name: Lichess
description: Completely free, ad-free, open source chess with analysis, puzzles and every variant you could want.

name: Nicky Case
description: Playable posts about game theory, mental health and emergence that treat you as a participant.

name: Koalas to the Max
description: A circle subdivides as your cursor moves, gradually revealing an image one quadrant at a time.

name: The A11Y Project
description: A community-driven checklist and pattern library that makes web accessibility approachable rather than scary.

name: GeoGebra
description: Free dynamic mathematics software for geometry, algebra, statistics and calculus, all in-browser.

name: City Roads
description: Renders every road in any city as a single elegant line drawing you can download and print.

name: time.is
description: The exact time anywhere, plus how far off your own clock is. Ugly, perfect, always right.

name: OpenStreetMap
description: The map of the world that anyone can edit, and that half the internet quietly runs on.

name: The Useless Web
description: One button. It sends you to a completely pointless website. That is the whole product.

name: Photopea
description: A full Photoshop-class image editor in a browser tab. Opens PSD, XCF, Sketch and RAW files.

name: Flexbox Froggy
description: Learn CSS flexbox by guiding frogs onto lily pads. Twenty-four levels and it finally sticks.

name: Refactoring Guru
description: Design patterns and refactorings explained with clear diagrams and code in a dozen languages.

name: Cover Your Tracks
description: The EFF tests how uniquely identifiable your browser fingerprint is. Sobering results.

name: A Soft Murmur
description: Mix rain, waves, wind and coffee shop noise into your own background soundscape.

name: Lobsters
description: A smaller, invite-only, tag-driven link aggregator with a notably high signal to noise ratio.

name: itch.io
description: An enormous, weird, wonderful marketplace for indie games, many of them free and playable in-browser.

name: Desmos Graphing Calculator
description: A graphing calculator so fast and pleasant that it turns algebra into doodling.

name: QuickRef.ME
description: Dense, well-organised cheat sheets for languages, tools and commands. The one you keep in a pinned tab.

name: Explorable Explanations
description: A hub for learning by playing: dozens of interactive essays on maths, society and systems.

name: regex101
description: Build, debug and explain regular expressions with a live match view and a step-by-step breakdown of every token.

name: Project Gutenberg
description: Seventy thousand public domain books, carefully proofread, in every format you would want.

name: The Quiet Place Project
description: A few small pages that ask you to stop, breathe and close all your other tabs for two minutes.

name: The True Size Of
description: Drag countries across the Mercator projection and watch Greenland shrink to its actual size.

name: Cat Bounce
description: Physics-enabled cats fall from the top of the screen. You can throw them. That is all.

name: Unsplash
description: High resolution photography under a permissive licence, with a search that mostly understands moods.

name: Scale of the Universe
description: Zoom continuously from the Planck length to the observable universe. Still stunning years later.

name: tldraw
description: An infinite canvas that feels impossibly smooth, with a genuinely delightful set of drawing primitives.

name: Fast.com
description: A speed test with no ads, no buttons and no upsell. It just starts measuring.

name: Incredibox
description: Drag sounds onto beatboxers to build a track. Somehow both a toy and a real instrument.

name: neal.fun
description: A collection of interactive toys and essays that are consistently the best thing on the internet that week.

name: musicForProgramming();
description: A long-running series of mixes selected specifically for staying in flow. No talking, no ads.

name: Exercism
description: Practice problems in seventy languages with free mentoring from real humans on your solutions.

name: roadmap.sh
description: Community-drawn learning roadmaps for frontend, backend, devops and more, with resources at every node.

name: Have I Been Pwned
description: Check whether your email has appeared in a known breach, from the person who catalogues them.

name: JSON Crack
description: Paste JSON, YAML or CSV and watch it explode into an interactive node graph you can actually read.

name: Hacker News
description: Link aggregator for programming and startups. Read the comments; that is where the value is.

name: The Wiki Game
description: Race other people from one Wikipedia article to another using only links. Surprisingly tense.

name: 3Blue1Brown
description: Mathematics with a visual soul: linear algebra, calculus and analysis animated into real intuition.

name: Bouncy Balls
description: Balls on the screen bounce to the noise level in your room. Teachers use it to quiet classrooms.

name: Bartosz Ciechanowski
description: Long, gorgeous interactive essays explaining how gears, cameras, GPS and light actually work.

name: Can I Use
description: Browser support tables for every web platform feature, with usage share so you know what you can actually ship.

name: Wayback Machine
description: Nine hundred billion saved web pages. The reason the internet has a memory at all.

name: Solar System Scope
description: An interactive, texture-accurate model of the planets that works beautifully as a teaching tool.

name: MarineTraffic
description: The same idea as Flightradar, but for ships. Watch global trade move in real time.

name: Hacker Typer
description: Mash the keyboard and produce convincing movie-hacker code. Best prank per byte on the web.

name: Google Fonts
description: Hundreds of open source families with fast previews, variable axes and a self-hosting download.

name: OverTheWire
description: Security wargames played over SSH, starting from absolute beginner. The classic on-ramp.

name: Excalidraw
description: A hand-drawn-feeling virtual whiteboard. Diagrams that look deliberately rough, shareable in one link.

name: Cleanup.pictures
description: Paint over an object in a photo and it disappears, with the background plausibly filled in.

name: Patatap
description: Every key on your keyboard triggers a sound and an animation. Instant synaesthesia.

name: Rijksstudio
description: Download seven hundred thousand works from the Rijksmuseum in extraordinary resolution, free to reuse.

name: Radiooooo
description: Pick a country and a decade and hear what was playing there. A time machine with a taste level.

name: The Odin Project
description: A full-stack curriculum that makes you build things rather than watch someone else build them.

name: Learn Git Branching
description: The best way to finally understand rebase: an animated, level-based sandbox for real git commands.

name: Distill
description: Beautifully typeset, interactive machine learning research. Archived, but still the high water mark.

name: CyberChef
description: The cyber swiss army knife: encode, decode, compress, hash and parse anything by dragging operations into a recipe.

name: Wiby
description: A search engine for pages built like it is still 1999. Surprise Me is the main feature.

name: Line Rider
description: Draw a track, watch a sledder ride it. Twenty years on, people still make music videos with it.

name: Internet Archive
description: Books, films, software, music and the web itself, preserved and free to access forever.

name: Sandspiel
description: A falling sand game with fire, water, plants and wind, plus a gallery of what everyone else made.

name: CSS Battle
description: Recreate a target image in as few bytes of CSS as possible. Competitive, humbling, weirdly addictive.

name: MDN Web Docs
description: The reference for HTML, CSS and JavaScript that actually gets updated. Documentation the whole web agrees on.
